chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about preparing for Ihram, so he said: In Masjid al-Shajara, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed in it. And I saw people making Ihram, so do not do it until you reach Al-Bayda', where the Mile, then you make Ihram as you are in your mounts.

Saying: 'Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Indeed, praise and grace are Yours, and dominion, You have no partner, here I am.' With convenience, with Umrah until Hajj.

key_terms.التَّهَيُّؤِ لِلْإِحْرَامِ: Preparing for the state of Ihram
key_terms.الْبَيْدَاءَ: Al-Bayda', a location near Medina serving as a Miqat
key_terms.الْمِيلُ: The Mile, a specific landmark or distance marker
key_terms.بِمَتَعٍ: With convenience or ease (referring to Tamattu' or general ease of ritual)
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: The opening phrase of the Talbiyah supplication
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الشَّجَرَةِ: Masjid al-Shajara, a specific mosque in Medina associated with the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Where is the correct place to enter Ihram when leaving Medina for Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani highlights the Shia preference for performing Ihram from the specific Miqat of Al-Bayda' rather than the local Masjid al-Shajara, emphasizing the practice of entering the state of Ihram while still on one's mount. The detailed recitation of the Talbiyah provided by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the importance of verbal declaration and specific wording in the ritual preparation for Hajj. This ruling reflects the broader scholarly discussion on whether the Miqat is a fixed geographical point or can be adapted based on the traveler's mode of transport and location.
